task_completion.description: Open the SeisComP Origin Locator (scolv) application.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The scolv main window is visible, showing the map and event list tabs.

task_completion.description: Create a new artificial origin using the coordinates and time from the alert file.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A dialog or input field in scolv showing Latitude: 37.498, Longitude: 137.242, and Depth: 10 km being entered.

task_completion.description: Commit the newly created origin to the database.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Commit' button is clicked or a 'Commit' dialog is shown, and the origin appears in the event list.

task_completion.description: Compute magnitudes using the archived waveform data from the GE network.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Magnitude' tab in scolv is active, showing calculated magnitude values (e.g., Mw, ML, or Mwp) for various stations.

task_completion.description: Commit the calculated magnitudes to the event.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The agent interacts with the 'Commit' action within the Magnitude tab; the magnitude value (likely > 7.0) is finalized.

task_completion.description: Export the complete event data to '~/recovered_event.xml'.
task_completion.visual_evidence: An export dialog or terminal command showing the event being saved to the specific path '/home/ga/recovered_event.xml'.

integrity.description: The agent used the scolv GUI for origin creation and magnitude calculation rather than just writing the XML manually.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the scolv interface being manipulated (mouse clicks on map, magnitude tab, or commit buttons).

integrity.description: The agent actually processed waveforms to get the magnitude.
integrity.visual_evidence: The scolv 'Magnitude' or 'Waveform' tabs show active traces or calculated amplitudes, not just a hardcoded magnitude value.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply rename an existing file to recovered_event.xml.
integrity.visual_evidence: The agent is seen using the 'Export' or 'Save' functionality within the SeisComP suite or a command-line tool like 'scxmldump'.
